name: Tillamook County
tax_rate: 10% county TLT in unincorporated areas plus 1% countywide inside cities; plus 1.5% state. Ordinance 74 Amendment 3 (10% to 14%) was referred to May 20, 2025 voters; result not confirmed in this research
deadline_pattern: Tourism Facilities Grants open mid-October and close December 15 each year; TAC scores in January, Board of County Commissioners approves in February. Separate TCVA Marketing Grants open January 1 and close late February
typical_open: Mid-October for facilities grants (October 15, 2025 for the 2025-26 cycle; 2026-27 open date listed as to be determined); January 1 for marketing and accessibility lodging grants
annual_pool: $400,000 Tourism Facilities Grants (max $75,000 per project) plus $100,000 TCVA Marketing Grants (max $10,000 per request; the October 2025 Pioneer article said $50,000 with $5,000 max, the November 2025 overview says $100,000 and $10,000) plus a new Accessibility Lodging Grant for hotels and motels
contact: Dan Haag, Tillamook Coast Visitors Association, dan@tillamookcoast.com, 503-842-2672 ext. 1 (facilities and marketing grants); Nan Devlin, TCVA Executive Director, nan@tillamookcoast.com, 503-842-2672 ext. 1
notes: Tillamook County splits its TLT 70% tourism / 30% roads and contracts the tourism share to the Tillamook Coast Visitors Association, which administers two grant rounds from it. The Tourism Facilities Grant ($400,000, up to $75,000, reimbursement only) is for improved real property with a 10-year life and is open only to governments, agencies and nonprofits; a nine-member volunteer Tourism Advisory Committee scores on a 105-point rubric (destination management 25, sustainability 20, collaboration 20, ROI 20, county income 20) and the Board of County Commissioners votes in February. Events fit better under the TCVA Marketing Grant (up to $10,000, businesses and nonprofits, must reach visitors traveling 50+ miles, scored by the TCVA board in March). No statement from the county about the 2027 HB 4148 effect was found.

name: Newport
tax_rate: 12% city (54% general government / 46% tourism); Lincoln County TLT applies only outside city limits; plus 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: Tourism Marketing Grant (Local Event Marketing Grant) has no fixed deadline: applications are due at least three months before the event and are taken up at the Destination Newport Committee's monthly meeting, then forwarded to City Council. The Destination Newport Grant lists an anticipated FY2025-26 pool but no deadline on the city page
typical_open: Open year-round; apply at least three months ahead of the event
annual_pool: Destination Newport Grant: up to $30,000 anticipated for FY2025-26. Tourism Marketing Grant Fund: no stated pool; council may fund all, part or none of a request
contact: Willow Ryon, grant inquiries (email on city grants page, obscured by Cloudflare); Erik Glover, Assistant City Manager/City Recorder, e.glover@newportoregon.gov, 541-574-0613; City Hall 541-574-0603
notes: Newport keeps 46% of its 12% room tax for tourism and runs its own DMO function (Discover Newport) through a city committee rather than a chamber contract. The Destination Newport Committee reviews event marketing grant requests at its monthly meeting and recommends to City Council; funds must be spent advertising outside Lincoln County, off-season (Sept 15 to June 15) events get priority, well-established events are generally not funded, and events in their first three years are preferred. The newer Destination Newport Grant (up to $30,000 for FY2025-26) names businesses as eligible and favors September-May and Sunday-Thursday overnight stays. A separate Tourism Facilities Grant application exists per the September 2024 committee agenda but its terms were not found. The committee is officially the Discover Newport Committee (seven members, one-year terms, NMC 2.05.045). The Tourism Facilities Grant, last documented in 2014, drew on a $100,000 Room Tax Fund contingency for 501(c) and government capital projects with a dollar-for-dollar match and a task force review with applicant presentations; the September 2024 committee agenda shows the application was being updated. In October 2024 the committee considered allocating $47,000 in remaining destination development funds.

The only published outside-applicant figure is the $30,000 Destination Newport Grant for FY2025-26; the Tourism Marketing Grant Fund has no stated pool.

name: Cottage Grove
tax_rate: 4% city (1 point passed through to the Chamber of Commerce) plus 5% Lane County plus 1.5% state; DOR-administered
deadline_pattern: No city grant round; the city passes 1% of its 4% room tax to the Cottage Grove Area Chamber of Commerce and receives an annual Lane County rural tourism allocation
annual_pool: None at city level; Cottage Grove received $52,061 from Lane County's 2026 rural tourism allocation ($553,172 countywide) and the chamber receives 1% of the city's 4% tax
contact: Georgia Haskell, Executive Director, Cottage Grove Area Chamber of Commerce
notes: Cottage Grove's 4% room tax predates the 2003 state restrictions and is structured to stay exempt from them; one percentage point goes to the chamber for visitor services and the rest to the general fund. The city's main tourism money is the Lane County rural tourism allocation ($52,061 for 2026, approved February 10, 2026) which the city spends on local tourism projects; Lane County also approved $500,000 in lodging tax for the covered bridges. Event organizers should approach the city and the chamber about the county allocation rather than expect an application round. The chamber director publicly opposed 2026 legislative changes to lodging tax use.
pool_note: City TLT about $119,000 with 1 of 4 points to the chamber; Lane County's 2026 rural tourism allocation to Cottage Grove is $52,061, spent at the city's discretion. No open application round.

name: Port Orford
tax_rate: 7% city plus Curry County TLT (10% in unincorporated areas) plus 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: City page says the TLT Committee meets once a year in July; in practice it met April 3, 2024, and April 24 and May 8, 2025 to review that year's applications, so expect a spring deadline
typical_open: Early spring; 2025 applications were on the May 8, 2025 committee agenda
annual_pool: Not published; awards are small (a $1,300 TLT grant disbursement appears in August 2023 financials)
contact: Port Orford City Hall (no grant contact listed on the TLT page)
notes: Port Orford runs a small TLT grant round from its 7% lodging tax. A volunteer TLT Committee (members must live within city limits) reviews applications in spring (April 3, 2024; April 24 and May 8, 2025) and recommends awards to City Council. Applicants have been very local: Port Orford Jubilee, Second Saturday, Historic Lindberg Home marker, visitor center mural, Sea Wolf Books native plant garden, Curry County Aquatic Safety, town guide and map, Mr. Ed's beautification. Pool and deadline are not published and individual awards appear to be in the low thousands; the city posts a TLT Grant Application Form and Instructions.

contact: City of Sweet Home Finance Department (Tax Administrator), 1140 12th Avenue, Sweet Home, OR 97386, 541-367-5128
notes: Sweet Home's 6% lodging tax dates to 1990 and the municipal code directs all collections to the General Fund; Ordinance 1335 (adopted June 24, 2025, effective July 24, 2025) modernized the chapter for short-term rentals and booking platforms but created no tourism set-aside, committee or grants. The Oregon Jamboree, the city's major event, is a registered lodging tax collector rather than a grant recipient. No outside-applicant funding exists at city level.

name: Coos County
tax_rate: No countywide TLT (10% countywide measure failed in 2015); county TLT applies only in the unincorporated Charleston area (9.5%); plus 1.5% state; DOR-administered since 2023
deadline_pattern: No county grant program; Charleston-area TLT is passed to the Coos Bay-North Bend VCB and Bandon Dunes pays a voluntary 6% assessment with 30% to Travel Southern Oregon Coast
notes: Coos County has no countywide lodging tax; voters rejected a 10% measure in 2015 after commissioners formed a stakeholder workgroup (VCB, Port of Coos Bay, Bandon Dunes, chambers, Coquille Tribe) to plan the 70% tourism share. The county collects TLT only in the Charleston area, which funds the Coos Bay-North Bend VCB, and Bandon Dunes pays a voluntary 6% assessment of which 30% goes to Travel Southern Oregon Coast. The input list notes a new 2026 county lodging-tax workgroup; that could not be confirmed in fetched sources. Events should apply to the VCB's $3,000 Tourism Grant instead.
pool_note: No countywide TLT; Charleston-area collections go to the VCB under agreement. No county dollars open to applicants.
